- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a price spike (e.g., 75+), especially in 30d horizon — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct — apply downward bias of 2–5% per day of negative sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/0.00 alternation, model tends to oscillate — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day average before final output.
